feedback.problem:
The equation

$$
(mx+10)(x+n)=-5{x}^{2}+20x-20
$$

is true for all values of $x,$ where $m$ and $n$ are constants. What is the value of $m+n?$

$m+n=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the equation is true for all values of $x,$ the expressions on both sides must be exactly the same. That means the product on the left-hand side must expand to match the right-hand side.

First, let's expand the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}(mx+10)(x+n) & =m{x}^{2}+mnx+10x+10n \\  & =m{x}^{2}+(mn+10)x+10n.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we equate the expanded form to the right-hand side:

$$
m{x}^{2}+(mn+10)x+10n=-5{x}^{2}+20x-20.
$$

Now, we compare the coefficients of corresponding terms.

- Equating the coefficients of ${x}^{2},$ we get

$$
m=-5.
$$

- Equating the constant terms, we get

$$
10n=-20\,⇒\,n=-2.
$$

Let's verify that values $m=-5$ and $n=-2$ produce the correct linear coefficient:

$$
\begin{aligned}mn+10 & =(-5)(-2)+10 \\  & =10+10 \\  & =20\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

which matches the coefficient of $x$ on the right-hand side. So, our solution is valid.

Finally, we compute the value of $m+n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m+n & =-5+(-2) \\  & =-7\end{aligned}
$$
